chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ali ibn Isma’il, on the authority of Ubaydullah al-Dihqan, who said: Musa ibn Ibrahim al-Marvazi informed me, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever memorizes from my nation forty traditions that they need regarding their religious affairs, God will raise him on the Day of Resurrection as a learned jurist.

Abu al-Hasan Tahir ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus ibn Hayyah al-Faqih informed me, in what he authorized for me in Balkh, saying: Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Harawi narrated to us, saying: Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hijr al-Sa’di narrated to us, saying: Sa’id ibn Najih narrated from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
Whoever memorizes from my nation forty traditions from the Sunnah, I will be his intercessor on the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for memorizing forty hadiths in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents two chains emphasizing the spiritual and intellectual rewards for preserving forty essential traditions, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the transmission of religious knowledge through specific chains of authority. The first chain promises the status of a learned jurist (faqih ‘alim), highlighting the practical necessity of understanding religious law, while the second offers the Prophet’s intercession, underscoring the metaphysical benefit of preserving the Sunnah. This practice serves as a foundational method for laypeople and scholars alike to secure both doctrinal competence and divine favor.
